item.title: Spring Authorization Server 1.5.7 Available Now
item.dc:creator: jgrandja
item.content:encoded:
On behalf of the team and everyone who has contributed, I am pleased to announce the availability of Spring Authorization Server 1.5.7.

This release addresses the following CVE:

  • CVE-2026-22752 "Spring Security Authorization Server Dynamic Client Registration endpoints perform insufficient validation of client metadata"

For a complete list of changes, refer to the changelog:

  • 1.5.7

Open source support for Spring Authorization Server 1.3.x, and 1.4.x generations has ended, see our support page for more information. Commercial customers can update to 1.3.11, or 1.4.10 respectively. These versions are available now on the Spring commercial artifact repository and can be accessed with a Spring Enterprise Subscription.

item.title: Spring Security 2026.04 Releases - Contains CVE Fixes
item.dc:creator: jzheaux
item.content:encoded:
On behalf of the team and everyone who has contributed, I am pleased to announce the availability of Spring Security 6.5.10, 7.0.5, and 7.1.0-RC1.

These releases address the following CVEs:

  • CVE-2026-22746 "User Attribute Enumeration when Using DaoAuthenticationProvider"
  • CVE-2026-22747 "Unauthorized User Impersonation when Using X.509 Client Certificates"
  • CVE-2026-22748 "Potential Security Misconfiguration when Using withIssuerLocation"
  • CVE-2026-22753 "Servlet Path Not Correctly Included in Path Matching of HttpSecurity#securityMatchers"
  • CVE-2026-22754 "Servlet Path Not Correctly Included in Path Matching of XML Authorization Rules"
  • CVE-2026-22752 "Spring Security Authorization Server Dynamic Client Registration endpoints perform insufficient validation of client metadata"
  • CVE-2026-22751 "Spring Security JdbcOneTimeTokenService allows a one-time token to authenticate multiple sessions"

For the 7.1.0-RC1 release, please check out the main feature set in our What's New in Spring Security 7.1 page.

For a complete list of changes, refer to the changelogs:

  • 6.5.10
  • 7.0.5
  • 7.1.0-RC1

Open source support for Spring Security 5.7.x, 5.8.x, 6.3.x, and 6.4.x generations has ended, see our support page for more information. Commercial customers can update to 5.7.23, 5.8.25, 6.3.16, or 6.4.16 respectively. These are also included in the latest Boot hot fixes, 2.7.32.2, 3.3.18.2, and 3.4.15.2. These versions are available now on the Spring commercial artifact repository and can be accessed with a Spring Enterprise Subscription.

item.title: Spring Integration 7.1.0-RC1 Available
item.dc:creator: cppwfs
item.content:encoded:
On behalf of the team and everyone who contributed, I am pleased to announce the release of Spring Integration 7.1.0-RC1.

Some notable changes in 7.1.0-RC1:

  • The RedisLockRegistry now uses native Redis CAS/CAD commands for lock renewal and release (Redis 8.4+), with automatic fallback to Lua scripts for older Redis versions.
  • The Redis module now provides a Java DSL API via its dedicated org.springframework.integration.redis.dsl.Redis factory.
  • The JmsChannelFactoryBean now allows users to set a custom JmsTemplate instead of using the default one.

See What's New in 7.1 for more details. Also, don't miss the Migration Guide for any observed breaking changes in this version.

This is the last chance to reach out to us on GitHub issues with any feedback before we go GA in May. Cheers, 
Glenn

item.title: This Week in Spring - April 21st, 2026
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded:
Hi Spring fans! Welcome to another installment of This Week in Spring!

What a week it's been since we last talked. I was in Barcelona, Spain, for the amazing Spring I/O event there. It has become my favorite show, full stop. Just such an amazing experience. So many wonderful things going on there. So many amazing community members. So much joy. And a little sangria, being 100% honest. Then, after that, I went and spent a little time in a beautiful village south of Barcelona, then I went to the south of France for a little fun in the sun. Then I went to two cities in lovely Poland, where I was thrilled to see some of the amazing community members. And now I'm winging my way to Paris, where I'll be presenting at Devoxx France and seeing some of the community there. And, yes, I did just speak at the Paris JUG not more than a few weeks ago. Later this week, Friday, I'll be in amazing Athens for the Devoxx Greece show, too! If you're about, don't forget to say hi!

  • This is so cool! Long-lived, memory sessions for Spring AI
  • I love this recipe from Spring AI in Action author Craig Walls on using Spring AI to enable A2A communication
  • And this one looking at the Spring AI TodoWriteTool
  • Want to use JSpecify and have it break your build when you're not in compliance, while using Apache Maven? Check this out!
  • I love this video from Netflix looking at how they use Java, Spring Boot, and Spring AI
  • This is super cool: branch-aware contract governance with Spring Cloud Contract
  • Nice! Spring Framework 7.1 will support compiling SpEL expressions that use java.util.Optional<T> with the null-safe and Elvis operators!
  • Spring Vault 4.1.0-RC1 and 4.0.2 released
  • Spring Data 2026.0.0 RC1 enters release candidate phase
  • Spring Data 2026.1.5 and 2025.0.11 released
  • Spring Framework 6.2.18 and 7.0.7 available now
